boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Sacramento State study settings, from reservable collaboration rooms and specialized library spaces to computer labs and after-hours work areas.

cards.title: Settle In Across Four Floors
cards.subtitle: Secure study space in the AIRC
cards.notes: Bring your OneCard for evening entry and check the live building-hours page before planning an overnight or holiday session.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor study option with secure after-hours access during the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State states that the AIRC provides four floors of secure study spaces and operates 24/7 during spring 2026 except holidays, with OneCard access required after 7 p.m.
cards.source_title: AIRC Building & IRT Service Desk Hours
cards.access_notes: Summer 2026 hours are Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m., through August 26; 24/7 operations then resume except holidays, with OneCard required after 7 p.m.

cards.title: Work With Course Software On Site
cards.subtitle: Computer-equipped workspace in AIRC 2004
cards.notes: Use this room when an assignment needs campus software or printing; account for the weekly Friday-night maintenance closure.
cards.short_summary: A staffed-campus alternative to working from a personal laptop.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State identifies AIRC 2004 as the IRT Computer Lab, lists it as a PrintSmart location, and documents installed course software including Adobe Creative Cloud, ArcGIS Pro, MATLAB, and SPSS.
cards.access_notes: The lab is listed as 24/7 except holidays, but closes each Friday at 7 p.m. until Saturday at 10 a.m. for maintenance; building access rules also apply.

cards.title: Pair Desk Work With Library Research
cards.subtitle: Second-floor computers and printing
cards.notes: Choose this lab for research sessions that need installed software or PrintSmart access, then confirm the current daily schedule.
cards.short_summary: A library-based computer workspace with broad weekday and weekend availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State lists LIB 2000 as a campus computer lab and separately identifies the Library second-floor computer lab as a black-and-white and color PrintSmart location.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Thursday 7:45 a.m.–11 p.m., Friday 7:45 a.m.–7 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; verify before arrival.

cards.title: Put the Shared Screen to Work
cards.subtitle: Twelve rooms for groups of two or more
cards.notes: Reserve with SacLink up to a week ahead, bring at least one partner, and arrive within 15 minutes to protect the booking.
cards.short_summary: Bookable collaboration rooms equipped for discussion and shared visual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library documents 12 group study rooms seating four to eight people, with Wi-Fi, power, flat screens, and whiteboards in all but rooms 135 and 3524.
cards.access_notes: SacLink login is required to reserve. Rooms are for groups of two or more, may be booked for up to two hours per day and one reservation per week, and are available when the library is open.

cards.title: Study With Children Close By
cards.subtitle: A family-equipped room for student parents and guardians
cards.notes: Check out the key with your child present, supervise throughout the visit, and restore the room’s setup before returning it.
cards.short_summary: A shared study room designed around the practical needs of student caregivers.
cards.evidence_claim: Library 2003 contains adult and child-sized tables and chairs, children’s books, a hand-washing station, power outlets, a play mat, and a play tent.
cards.access_notes: Limited to eligible Sacramento State student parents or guardians with a child present at key checkout. First come, first served; up to four hours, once daily; two families maximum.

cards.title: Rehearse With the Camera Running
cards.subtitle: A reservable recording and presentation studio
cards.notes: Reserve ahead, bring a laptop for the wall display, and use a USB drive to take your rehearsal recording with you.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built place to refine a class talk, conference presentation, or interview.
cards.evidence_claim: The room provides a large wall display, wall-mounted camera, confidence monitor, studio lights, green screen, and dedicated USB storage for presentation recordings.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required. The room is available to Sacramento State students, faculty, and staff during applicable library access hours.

cards.title: Take a Virtual Class Behind a Door
cards.subtitle: Individual rooms intended for Zoom sessions
cards.notes: Bring a current OneCard, request a key at the Service Desk, and return it early if the session ends before the three-hour loan expires.
cards.short_summary: A controlled setting for attending an online class while on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library describes its Zoom Rooms as quiet spaces for viewing Zoom sessions and makes them available to currently enrolled students through key checkout.
cards.access_notes: Current OneCard required. Keys are first come, first served for three hours, may be renewed if available, cannot be reserved, and must be returned by closing.

cards.title: Choose Between a Carrel and a Group Table
cards.subtitle: Specialized collection room with multiple work settings
cards.notes: Use a carrel for focused reading or a table for collaborative research, with collection materials and computers close at hand.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive reading room combining individual, collaborative, and computer workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 3034 houses most of the Tsakopoulos Hellenic Collection and includes individual study carrels, group-study tables, computers, and exhibit cases.
cards.access_notes: The collection room is accessible during the same hours as the main University Library building.

cards.title: Work Beside Ready Reference Shelves
cards.subtitle: Reference room adjoining the Hellenic Collection
cards.notes: Set up here when dictionaries, encyclopedias, atlases, or current journals can support the research without leaving the room.
cards.short_summary: A reference-focused setting suited to source-heavy reading and note taking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library identifies Room 3024 as the Tsakopoulos Reference Collection, adjacent to Room 3034 and housing non-circulating current journals and reference materials.
cards.access_notes: The reference room follows the main University Library building hours; materials described there are non-circulating and should remain in the room.

cards.title: Check Out a Room for Solo Work
cards.subtitle: Six individual rooms in the University Library
cards.notes: Bring a valid OneCard and request a key at the first-floor Service Desk before heading upstairs for an individual session.
cards.short_summary: Key-controlled rooms for students who need separation from open study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library documents six individual study rooms on its fourth floor, with keys available from the first-floor Service Desk to users with a valid OneCard.
cards.access_notes: Valid OneCard required for key checkout at the first-floor Service Desk. The rooms are available only while the University Library is open.
